notes: Site is a client-rendered WCS/PWA (Akamai-protected); direct curl_cffi HTTP fetch of the homepage/PLP HTML only returns a preloader shell, so Playwright (channel=chrome, real Chrome binary) was used once to capture the site's own internal JSON APIs from network traffic, then all discovery/qty pulls were done with plain HTTP requests (curl_cffi, Chrome impersonation) against those same endpoints (no bot-challenge issues once channel=chrome fingerprint was used): JSONAPIs?module=categories (top nav), JSONAPIs?module=subCategories&categoryId=N&apiVersion=2 (full nav subtree incl. subsubcategories), and UnbxdAPI?categoryId=N&rows=... (exact numberOfProducts per category, cross-checked against each response's own unbxdQuery categoryPath to confirm the id maps to the intended node, not a stale/duplicate one - this caught one wrong-id trap, see below). robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Checked top nav (whats-new/outdoor/indoor-furniture/bed-bath/lighting-decor/rugs-pillows/tabletop-entertaining/holiday-decor/sale) - the only seasonal root is 'Holiday Decor & Gifts' (categoryId 12051, 586 products total), which is almost entirely Christmas-themed (Christmas Trees, Wreaths & Garlands, Ornaments, Christmas Decor, Outdoor [Christmas] Decor, Christmas Storage, Holiday Entertaining whose own H1 override is literally 'Christmas Table Decor'). Excluded from that hub: 'All Holiday Decor' (subCatId 165151, page title 'All Frontgate Holiday Decor & Christmas Decor') - a View-All aggregator whose 6 children duplicate the main tree's own top-level categories by name (Christmas Trees/Wreaths & Garlands/Ornaments/Outdoor Decor/Christmas Decor/Christmas Storage) at the same level - kept the main tree only per the overlap rule. 'Gifts' (subCatId 144214, page <title> 'Christmas Gifts for the Home') was investigated and excluded: its own H1 override is generic ('Home Decor Gifts'), its meta description is non-holiday ('gifts for the home...game room games...Resort Collection towels'), and all 4 real children's own page titles are non-holiday-specific ('Our Most Popular Holiday Gifts' = Best-Sellers-style curation, 'Luxury Housewarming Gifts', 'Outdoor Gifts & Outdoor Decor Gifts', 'Party Host & Hostess Gifts') - only the parent's SEO title uses 'Christmas', so this reads as a general gift shop cross-merchandised under the holiday nav rather than a genuine seasonal category (rules SS5-6). Also excluded under this hub: 'Discover' subtree (New Arrivals, Tree Quiz, Holiday Guide - all marketing/tool/editorial pages) and 'Holiday Clearance' (a Sale/Clearance page). A separate top-level 'Halloween' page exists (categoryId 124679, found via a Google site: search, not linked in the visible main nav) but its own UnbxdAPI response returns an empty product grid (numberOfProducts 0, empty products/facets) and the rendered page shows no content beyond the breadcrumb as of this check (2026-09-03) - genuinely 0 products right now, so per the 0-qty-drop rule no row is written for it, though the category slot exists in the site's taxonomy. A 'Fall Decor' node is cross-listed under both the Holiday Decor hub (subCatId 250161, dead alias returning 0 products - categoryPath mismatch) and under New & Trending > Trending (subCatId 216166, the live/canonical id, categoryPath 'New & Trending>Trending>Fall Decor', 106 products, canonical URL /whats-new/seasonal-favorites/seasonal-decor/, sample product 'Ember Glow Wreath' - 'captures the beauty of fall'); the working id/URL was kept as a genuine Autumn/Fall seasonal category. Ran WebSearch site:frontgate.com checks for Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, Easter, and Diwali - no dedicated category/PLP pages surfaced for any of them (only blog/editorial 'Home + Style' tag pages, isolated unrelated PDPs, or other retailers' results), consistent with no such nav branches existing on the site; recorded as absent, not fabricated. Overlap rule applied to Wreaths & Garlands / Christmas Decor / Outdoor Decor parents: each has its own real Unbxd product count (96 / 200 / 69) but its own listed children only partially/overlappingly cover that count (e.g. Wreaths+Garlands+Swags+Topiaries = 107 vs parent 96), so each parent was kept as a grouping row (qty null) with the site's own parent count noted in its flag, to avoid double-counting against the child rows.
